preparation: Provide a legible actual Canada political map/current capital table and the13attributed regional resource rows. Point out the2021date and the simplified qualitative use of the statistical source. Do not turn percentages or ethnic lists into a new memorization curriculum.

Prepare an age-appropriate selected narrative from Maxime Morin’s attributed contemporary community account and its actual speaker/location information. It complements the regional examples; it does not speak for every member of a people.
actions: After study, complete the independent political-geography claim: name/locate all13divisions and capitals, distinguish province/territory/national capital roles, and recognize them in a changed map style. Retain the prior no-answer-label check; a resource lookup is not a replacement for that whole claim.

For EACH province and territory, use the attributed row alongside the actual map to describe its broad location and identify some peoples whose residents were reported there in2021. Say explicitly that the examples are neither all residents nor people exclusive to that region; First Nations, Métis and Inuit are distinct peoples with diverse communities. Resource-supported description is acceptable; no universal rote ethnic inventory is imposed.

Explain why an Inuit person may live outside Nunavut and why a province or capital name cannot tell you a particular resident’s identity. The table provides examples of residence, not traditional territory boundaries, citizenship adjudication or cultural behaviour.

Listen/read the selected Métis narrator’s actual account, identify the speaker and Saskatchewan case, and explain that this particular experience does not establish what every Métis person experiences. Independently name the three distinct Indigenous peoples and their continuing present-day communities, preserving the complete existing Lcqm claim.

Transfer by describing the location and source-attributed peoples examples for a differently ordered region on another accurate map; distinguish an unsupported identity/generalization from the source-supported limited description.
protocol.positive: Complete map/capital knowledge plus actual resource-supported peoples/location descriptions for all13regions, with distinct peoples, contemporary diversity and attributed perspective limits.
nearMiss: Names all capitals but gives no peoples/location description for several regions.
Says every resident of Nunavut is Inuit or only Nunavut has Inuit residents.
Infers a person’s identity or traditional territory from a provincial label.
Uses an individual interview as the voice of all Métis people.
